notes:
24429 shooting incidents on 7548 days, 2006-01-01 to 2026-08-31 (5ucz-vwe8, one row per incident). The archived file 833y-fsy8 agrees to within 2 incidents for 2006-2024 ({'sum_5ucz': 23300, 'sum_833y': 23298, 'days_differ': 6}). Sensitivity analyses all lie between 1.11 and 1.17 per 5 C (lag 0-1, TMIN, May-September, 2006-2019, 2020-2026, murder incidents). The graph has no relationship between gun violence and temperature; its temperature-homicide rows contain two mis-extractions: Xu 2020 percent increases stored as odds ratios 0.095 and 0.088 (absent from the Dataverse CSV) and Rahman 2023 percent increases stored as odds ratios 4.9 and 6.2 (present in the CSV). The NYC estimate lies between the homicide estimates (1.05-1.10) and the Chicago shootings estimates (1.16-1.19).

After the referee of heat-night-minimum (13 Nov 2026): the registered count is by calendar date, and 35% of New York shooting incidents occur between 00:00 and 05:59, before the maximum of the date they are counted on. The referee of heat-night-minimum raised this. With each shooting assigned to the day whose night it falls in (06:00 on date d to 05:59 on d+1), the registered model gives 1.135 (1.118 to 1.152) per 5 C against 1.146 (1.130 to 1.163) on calendar dates (7,547 days, 24,424 incidents). The registered condition, a lower limit above 1.00, is met either way, and the estimate stays inside the registered 1.05 to 1.20. The average slope therefore does not depend on the assignment. The hot end does: with the piecewise-linear basis of round 2 the ratio 33 against 27 C is 1.051 (0.988 to 1.118) on night-of counts against 1.102 (1.038 to 1.171) on calendar dates, and with the 4-df cubic spline of this claim it is 1.090 (1.041 to 1.141) against 1.122 (1.072 to 1.173). A quarter to a half of the log rise above 27 C on calendar dates therefore comes from the assignment of small-hours shootings to the hot date. Exploratory, run after the outcomes, and deciding nothing under rule 4 (analyses/critique/round5_night_of_check.py; data/derived/round5/heat_night/night_of_check.json).
